questions.text: Let [latex]G[/latex] be an undirected connected graph in which every edge has a positive integer weight.  Suppose  that  every  spanning  tree  in  [latex]G[/latex]  has  even  weight.  Which  of  the following statements is/are TRUE for every such graph [latex]G[/latex] ?
questions.solution:
Take any cycle C and two edges [latex]e,f[/latex] on it. Extend the path [latex]C-f[/latex] to a spanning tree T (it contains [latex]e[/latex], not [latex]f[/latex]). Then [latex]T'=T-e+f[/latex] is also a spanning tree.

[latex]w(T')-w(T)=w(f)-w(e)[/latex]. Both trees are even, so [latex]w(f)-w(e)[/latex] is even [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]e[/latex] and [latex]f[/latex] have the same parity. So in every cycle all edges are even or all are odd [latex]\text{---}[/latex] TRUE.

Counter-examples for the rest:
- Triangle with all weights 1: every spanning tree has weight 2 (even), yet edges are odd [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] options 1 and 3 FALSE.
- Path with weights 1, 1, 2: only spanning tree has weight 4, but edges are mixed [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] option 2 FALSE.

Answer: In each cycle, either all edges have even weight OR all edges have odd weight

questions.text:
Consider a context-free grammar [latex] G [/latex] with the following 3 rules.
[latex] S \rightarrow a S, S \rightarrow a S b S, S \rightarrow c [/latex]
Let [latex] w \in L(G) [/latex]. Let [latex] n_a(w), n_b(w), n_c(w) [/latex] denote the number of times [latex] a, b, c [/latex] occur in [latex] w [/latex], respectively. Which of the following statements is/are TRUE?
questions.solution:
Count symbols contributed by each rule:
- Every S finally becomes one c. [latex]S\rightarrow aSbS[/latex] adds one b and one extra S; [latex]S\rightarrow aS[/latex] adds no S. Starting with one S: [latex]n_c=n_b+1[/latex] [latex]\text{---}[/latex] TRUE (so [latex]n_c=2n_b[/latex] is FALSE, e.g. w = c).
- Each b comes with an a, so [latex]n_a\ge n_b=n_c-1 \gt n_c-2[/latex] [latex]\text{---}[/latex] TRUE.
- [latex]n_a \gt n_b[/latex] fails for w = acbc ([latex]n_a=n_b=1[/latex]) [latex]\text{---}[/latex] FALSE.

Answer: [latex]n_a(w) \gt n_c(w)-2[/latex] and [latex]n_c(w)=n_b(w)+1[/latex]

questions.text:
Consider a disk with the following specifications: rotation speed of 6000 RPM,
average seek time of 5 milliseconds, 500 sectors/track, 512-byte sectors.
A file has content stored in 3000 sectors located randomly on the disk. Assuming
average rotational latency, the total time (in seconds, rounded off to 2 decimal
places) to read the entire file from the disk is _______
questions.solution:
6000 RPM = 100 rotations/s [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] one rotation = 10 ms, average rotational latency = 5 ms.
Transfer time of one sector [latex]=10/500=0.02[/latex] ms.

Sectors are random, so each needs seek + latency + transfer:
[latex]5+5+0.02=10.02[/latex] ms

Total [latex]=3000\times10.02\text{ ms}=30.06[/latex] s

Answer: 30.06

questions.text:
Consider a TCP connection operating at a point of time with the congestion window
of size 12 MSS (Maximum Segment Size), when a timeout occurs due to packet
loss. Assuming that all the segments transmitted in the next two RTTs (Round Trip
Time) are acknowledged correctly, the congestion window size (in MSS) during the
third RTT will be _________
questions.solution:
On timeout: [latex]ssthresh=12/2=6[/latex] MSS and cwnd resets to 1 MSS, then slow start (doubling each RTT):

- RTT 1: cwnd = 1
- RTT 2: cwnd = 2
- RTT 3: cwnd = 4 (still below ssthresh = 6)

Answer: 4

questions.text:
Consider an Ethernet segment with a transmission speed of [latex]10^8[/latex] bits/sec and a
maximum segment length of 500 meters. If the speed of propagation of the signal
in the medium is [latex]2 \times 10^8[/latex] meters/sec, then the minimum frame size (in bits) required
for collision detection is _________
questions.solution:
For collision detection, transmission time must be at least the round-trip propagation time: [latex]\frac{L}{B}\ge2\frac{d}{v}[/latex]

[latex]T_p=\dfrac{500}{2\times10^8}=2.5\ \mu s[/latex]

[latex]L=2\times2.5\times10^{-6}\times10^8=500[/latex] bits

Answer: 500
